hook: A tunnel under the national library in Buenos Aires, lined with books that almost exist: familiar authors with works they never wrote, and anonymous volumes in every language. Most of the file is a catalog of these finds, so it reads like browsing very strange shelves. Expect wordplay and literary in-jokes rather than danger.
whyItMatters: SCP-1986 wears its inspiration openly, with a footnote pointing to Jorge Luis Borges and his story about an infinite library, and it sets the anomaly in the same library where the file says Borges worked. It is a Safe-class article that exists mostly for the pleasure of its ideas, showing that the format can be playful and bookish instead of frightening. The recovered-works list is the main attraction and is built for dipping in and out of.
thingsToNotice: Treat each catalog entry as a tiny story: the joke often lives in a single constraint, like a poetry collection that avoids one letter or a naval reference written entirely in limericks. Several entries sketch whole alternate histories in a sentence or two, giving the tunnel a depth beyond its measured kilometres. The footnotes reward attention as well, from the topology aside to a researcher's comparison between browsing the shelves and hunting for rational numbers along the real line. Notice how calm the containment section is; nothing here threatens anyone, and the article knows it.

related.note: Another book-centred file whose pages record histories that split away from ours.
